headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage: aci can egress to SaaS APIs while awesome-python is non-runnable and networkless, so most pairwise harms are limited by B's lack of execution surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default communication channel is documented between aci and awesome-python. aci can call APIs and use MCP, but awesome-python is not runnable and exposes no I/O surfaces, so there is no evidence B can ingest A's outputs as instructions.
conditions: IF awesome-python is wrapped in a runtime that reads aci output from a shared channel, injection becomes possible.
IF an operator manually copy-pastes aci output into another agent, prompt injection risk appears.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared chat or clipboard channels.
Do not pipe aci outputs into any parser that executes instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any future shared message bus.

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress, so it can transmit sensitive context to third-party services. awesome-python is non-runnable and networkless, so it does not add a second exfiltration path, but the pair still exposes aci-held data to external APIs in default use.
conditions: IF aci is connected to live CRM or email accounts, sensitive records can flow to external APIs.
IF awesome-python is replaced with a runnable agent that shares the same workspace, leakage scope increases.
mitigations: Restrict aci to non-sensitive test data.
Disable or narrow external API connectors not needed for the task.
Review OAuth scopes before enabling live integrations.
Keep awesome-python as a read-only reference artifact.
requires-engineering: add DLP or redaction before any outbound call.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and broad API access, but awesome-python is not runnable and has no write surfaces or scopes. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; any conflict would require unusual orchestration not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF awesome-python is embedded into a writable runtime with shared credentials, overlapping writes could occur.
IF aci instances are pointed at the same mutable CRM or calendar account, race conditions may appear.
mitigations: Assign separate test accounts to each agent.
Avoid concurrent writes from multiple aci instances.
Use a single-writer policy for shared SaaS resources.
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency controls.

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM, email, and scheduling actions, but awesome-python is only a non-runnable collection and cannot automatically consume or act on aci output. The pair therefore lacks a documented default chain where B blindly executes A's results.
conditions: IF awesome-python is replaced by an executor that trusts aci output, cascading errors become possible.
IF an operator manually uses aci-generated text as authoritative without review, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before any email or CRM action.
Treat aci output as draft content only.
Do not automate commits from aci-generated text.
requires-engineering: add verification steps before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: aci touches email, CRM, calendar, and support data, which can carry residency or retention obligations, while awesome-python touches no data and has no runtime. The compliance risk is therefore one-sided and limited to aci's external integrations rather than a pairwise mismatch.
conditions: IF aci is used with regulated customer data, retention and residency controls must be checked.
IF a future runnable B handles the same data class under different policies, mismatch risk increases.
mitigations: Limit aci to non-regulated datasets.
Confirm retention settings on connected SaaS apps.
Document data residency for each connector.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement per connector.
